newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Burundi minister says over 30,000 refugees return.
newsitem.headline: Burundi minister says over 30,000 refugees return.

text.p: Burundian Prime Minister Pascal Firmin Ndimira said on Tuesday that more than 30,000 refugees out of an estimated 150,000 had returned from eastern Zaire.
The Burundian Hutu refugees fled Burundi two years ago to escape violence and death following the massacre of up to a million Tutsis in neighbouring Rwanda.
"The return began spontaneously," Ndimira, who heads Burundi's transitional government, told reporters after talks with EU Development Aid Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro.
"We need food and logistical aid as Burundi is under an embargo and we suffer from a fuel shortage," he added.
Regional states led by Kenya and Tanzania imposed sanctions on Burundi six days after Tutsi military leader Pierre Buyoya seized power on July 25.
Asked whether an international force was needed in his country, Ndimira said, "A military presence is unnecessary on Burundian soil but humanitarian aid is most welcome."

On Tuesday, Western European Union (WEU) foreign and defence ministers meeting in Ostend, Belgium, said they were willing to provide air and logistics support for a humanitarian aid effort in Africa's troubled Great Lakes region.
Ndimira said he informed the EU of the situation in Burundi.
"There is a net improvement in security in towns and some rural areas," he said, adding however that armed rebels were causing difficulties in some regions.

In Nairobi, diplomats and senior Burundian officials said on Tuesday that Burundian Hutu rebels, driven out of refugee camps in eastern Zaire, were regrouping in Tanzania after fighting their way across Burundi.
